item.title: LaView Galaxy Projector review
item.description: This premium projector is packed with features, but the LaView Galaxy Projector doesn’t quite match up to its rivals.

item.title: In the search for bees, Mozambique honey hunters and birds share a language with distinct, regional dialects
item.description: People searching for honey in Mozambique work with birds via a shared language in a rare case of cooperation between humans and wild animals. This language also comes with regional dialects — that appear to be driven by the birds.

item.title: 'System in flux': Scientists reveal what happened when wolves and cougars returned to Yellowstone
item.description: Large carnivores are both clashing and coexisting in the western United States. Although wolves dominate cougars and steal their prey, cougars' shift from elk- to deer-heavy diets, paired with a rugged landscape for escape, might help cougars avoid violent wolf encounters.

item.title: Mokoqi Star Projector Night Light review
item.description: The Mokoqi Star Projector is a cheerful, low-cost sleep aid for babies and tots.

item.title: 'Landmark' elephant bone finding in Spain may be from time of Hannibal's war against Rome
item.description: An elephant bone discovered in Spain may date to the time of Hannibal's battles against the Romans.

item.title: Hydrogen leak derails Artemis II wet rehearsal, pushing launch date back by weeks
item.description: NASA has delayed the Artemis II launch until March at the earliest after engineers discovered hydrogen leaks during last night's wet dress rehearsal.

item.title: Men develop cardiovascular disease 7 years before women, study suggests. But why?
item.description: Men's heart health tends to decline earlier in life, and the difference is driven largely by coronary heart disease, which appears roughly a decade sooner in men than in women.

item.title: Asteroid 2024 YR4's collision with the moon could create a flash visible from Earth, study finds
item.description: If the building-size asteroid 2024 YR4 crashes into the moon in December 2032, the impact will produce a bright flash that may be visible to the naked eye, a new study finds.

item.title: Grim photo captures polar bear mom and cubs resting in mud in summer heat
item.description: An image of polar bears napping along the Hudson Bay coast in Canada has been shortlisted for the Wildlife Photographer of the Year Nuveen People's Choice Award 2026.
